html:
St Lucia became independent from Britain on 22 February 1979, with John Compton as its first prime minister. He led the island for most of the next three decades.

The island had been fought over by France and Britain for two centuries, until the British won it for good in 1814, after the wars of the 1700s. Sugar estates worked by enslaved Africans gave way after emancipation to small farms; indentured Indians arrived from 1859.

In the late 20th century bananas sold to Britain were the main export, then tourism took over. The country is part of the Commonwealth, with the British monarch as head of state.
